components.name: The Record
components.description: A static impression of the signature disc: cherry vinyl, one hot white and one hot yellow groove, cobalt label, yellow spindle. The real one is a Metal shader.

narrative.overview:
The window is a single record, seen from directly above, too big for its frame. Everything said in the conversation is physically cut into it: your voice in white, the reply in yellow, spiralling outward from the label as a calendar of what was said. There is nothing to press. Clicking anywhere drops the arm; dragging around the disc scratches back through the talk.

The surface is loud and flat like a pressed sleeve. Colour runs at full strength over the whole window, heavy geometric type is printed straight onto the vinyl, and one colour change from across the room tells you the phase. Density is low on the stage: one status word, the words being said, a line of underlined controls and a line of small print. Depth comes from the record itself, not from interface layers.

The whole of it is driven by one mechanism. Rotation, groove age and a single travelling wavefront account for all stage motion, drawn by one Metal fragment shader, so a long conversation costs the GPU the same as a short one. The world refuses the category's glowing blob and round mic button. Settings is deliberately outside the world: native macOS forms with cherry accents.
keyCharacteristics: Full-strength cherry vinyl bleeding past every edge, with a cobalt label
White ink for you and yellow ink for the reply, on grooves, words and cartridge alike
Grooves that start hot and big, then cool and sink back into the vinyl
One wavefront carrying each change across the whole surface
Heavy type set directly on the vinyl, with no cards, pills or glass on the stage
Underlined words as controls, and the whole window as the talk control

rules.name: The Whole Disc Rule
rules.body: A phase colour changes the entire vinyl, never a badge, dot or patch on it. The state should read from across the room.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: In grooves, spoken words and the cartridge, white is always you and yellow is always the reply. Yellow never carries interface text on the vinyl.

rules.name: The Full Strength Rule
rules.body: Words on the vinyl are pure white or pure yellow at full opacity. Yellow on cherry reaches 4.3:1, so it is set at 21pt or larger; white on cherry reaches 4.7:1. The only lowered values are disabled controls (50 to 55%) and the empty type field's prompt (80%, at 22pt). A line you cut off is still drawn at 72% in the build, which falls to 2.7:1 on cherry: that is a defect to fix, not a state to copy.

rules.name: The Whole String Rule
rules.body: Avenir Next has no Cyrillic, so any string containing an alphabetic character at or above U+0250 is set entirely in the system face at the same size and weight. Never let Avenir's punctuation mix into another script, and pass the string to the font choice wherever the text is user or model content.

rules.name: The Size by Length Rule
rules.body: On the vinyl, text size follows length (34, 26, then 21pt) rather than role, so a short answer shouts and a long one still fits.

rules.name: The Tonearm Rule
rules.body: The arm is the only object that floats above the record. Interface elements stay printed on it.

rules.name: The Hot Groove Rule
rules.body: Only the groove being cut stands out. Anything older must cool into the vinyl, so the disc stays calm however long the talk runs.

rules.name: The One Front Rule
rules.body: One wavefront crosses the disc at a time, at 1400pt a second from the centre, with the new colour inside it and the old one outside. A vinyl or label colour change strikes at full strength, entering hearing or speaking from a calm phase strikes at 0.6, and cutting into a reply strikes at 2.4 with no colour change. Phase changes that alter neither colour nor strike state send nothing.

rules.name: The Word Is the Control Rule
rules.body: Stage controls are underlined words. Icon-only buttons are kept to the top bar, the actions under a reply and the composer toggles. Nothing on the stage is a filled or pill-shaped button.

rules.name: The No Mic Button Rule
rules.body: Talking starts from a click on the window or floating record, Space, the global shortcut or the menu bar item, never from a dedicated button in the window. Mute mic is a word, and it appears only once the mic is on.

rules.name: The Native Settings Rule
rules.body: Settings is where the app stops performing. Add the cherry tint and the display-face header, and leave the rest to the system.

dos: Do derive every moving part of the stage from the record's one mechanism: rotation, groove age and the wavefront.
Do drive grooves from the sound actually happening, in the owner's ink.
Do change state by changing the whole vinyl, and pair it with its status word.
Do set text straight on the vinyl in pure white or yellow, with the grooves hushed behind it.
Do use the system face for the whole string when text contains any non-Latin script.
Do make a new stage control an underlined word (Text Action).
Do keep Settings native, adding only the cherry tint and the pane header.
Do respect Reduce Motion and pause drawing when idle or hidden: the language model needs the GPU.
donts: Don't add a glowing orb or blob, or a round mic button.
Don't put cards, pills or glass on the stage. The floating record's strips exist only because it has no vinyl beneath its text.
Don't add shadows to text or controls. The tonearm's shadow is the record's own.
Don't set yellow text on cherry below 21pt.
Don't dim words on the vinyl to show hierarchy; change size or weight, or move them to the sleeve.
Don't let old grooves stay bright, or add a second concurrent wavefront.
Don't add a button to start talking.
